note: The exposure-owner experiment half worked. Serializing it did stop the cancellation, and the owner MEASURED the pipeline rather than deriving it — a ramp of Lambertian patches rendered through the real chain, fitted to a closed-form model at RMS 0.7-1.3/255, published as an albedo->display table. But it solved the flesh against the CAMERA-FACING irradiance (E=0.704) while the dramatic key-facing case (E=1.565) still blows out, so the key-lit cut face is unchanged at 49.3% clipped. A contract fixes coordination; it does not by itself pick the right load case. Gains are also decelerating (+0 to +9, mean +4.2 against last round's +10) and three pieces are now blocked on files they do not own. The biggest of those was fixed by hand afterwards: director.js spawned uniform-random orientations, throwing away the silhouette geometry.js had authored — flagged by the critic three rounds running. Biasing the long axis toward the screen plane took the hero aspect from 1.000 to 0.784 and max protrusion from 18.3% to 28.3%.

pieces.name: Lighting, grade & DOF
pieces.biggestGap: The lens only exists on opaque geometry: the entire transparent particle layer bypasses DOF by design, so in 00-hero -- the money shot, which contains exactly one opaque object -- 141 droplets spanning a 6x range of apparent diameter (4->26 px) all render at 1.46-1.75 px 10-90 edge, statistically identical to the in-focus melon's 1.55 px, i.e. the hero frame has no lens at all.
pieces.fix: src/render/stage.js. The gather takes CoC from the opaque depth buffer only, and the sprite pass is depthWrite:false, so every droplet inherits the depth of whatever is behind it -- void -> CoC 0. Give the sprites their own CoC channel and take cocEff = max(opaqueCoC, particleCoC): add one half-res
